descriptionChirho: The noun βρῶσις in its primary sense of food or nourishment — the substance that is eaten, sustenance. This is the dominant usage (7 occurrences), referring to food as a concrete object (e.g., 'My flesh is true food'). Multilingual glosses consistently point to food-as-substance: Arabic طَعَام (food/sustenance), Hindi भोजन (meal/food), Korean 음식 (food), Spanish comida/alimento (food/nourishment), Swahili chakula (food). Distinct from the act of eating and from the metaphorical decay sense.

The noun βρῶσις in its metaphorical sense of rust, corrosion, or moth-eating — the destructive consuming of material goods, as in Matt 6:19-20 where treasures are destroyed by moth and rust. This is a genuinely distinct semantic extension from 'eating' to 'being eaten away/corroded.' Multilingual glosses sharply distinguish this: Spanish herrumbre (rust), Hindi जंग (rust/corrosion), Arabic صَدَأ (rust), Korean 녹 (rust), Swahili kutu (rust). No overlap with the food or eating senses.

The noun βρῶσις denoting the act or process of eating itself, as distinct from the food eaten. Used in contexts discussing dietary practices or the activity of consuming food (e.g., Rom 14:17 'the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking'). Multilingual glosses distinguish the action from the substance: Arabic أَكْل (eating, verbal noun), Hindi खाना/खाने (eating/to eat), Korean 먹는–것/먹기 (the act of eating), Spanish comer (to eat, verbal), Swahili kula (to eat). This process/action sense contrasts with βρῶσις as food-substance.
